why: The criterion holds for both checks. Check 1 passes on "output contains `BAD {}`… and loadConfig is defined in src/config.js". It fails on `THREW`, on a non-`{}` result, or if loadConfig is missing from src/config.js. All of that comes from the expect line: loadConfig in src/config.js has to catch the JSON.parse error and return {}. The stricter checks sit under Advisory and are kept out of PASS and FAIL. Those are valid files still parsing, missing files still throwing, the test being replaced rather than deleted, the stderr message, and the README. Check 2 passes when "the test run reports no failing tests (`# fail 0`)". It fails when any test fails or the command can't run. That matches "npm test passes" without adding anything stricter. Neither condition requires a mutation test, a branch or file-scope rule, or exact wording.
